questions.question: What is the norm of hash_embed("cat", dim=256)?
options: Exactly 256
The number of tokens in text
Approximately 1
Always 0
questions.explanation: hash_embed accumulates signed hash buckets and divides by the Euclidean norm when it is nonzero.

questions.question: What range can hash_token("cat", dim=256) return?
options: Only -1 or 1
A floating-point cosine score
An integer from 1 through 256
An integer from 0 through 255
questions.explanation: The hash integer is reduced with modulo dim, producing indices 0 <= idx < 256.

questions.question: What happens when two tokens hash to the same embedding bucket?
options: Their signed contributions add in that coordinate
One token is discarded from the text
The dimension automatically doubles
The entire vector is replaced with zeros
questions.explanation: The hash trick permits collisions; hash_embed adds each token contribution into its selected coordinate.

questions.question: What does truncate_matryoshka(vec, new_dim=64) do after slicing?
options: It pads the vector back to 256 values
It renormalizes the first 64 values to unit length when their norm is nonzero
It sorts the values by magnitude before returning
It converts the slice into token counts
questions.explanation: The helper takes vec[:new_dim], computes its norm, and divides by that norm unless it is zero.

questions.question: What score does sparse_score give to two token-count Counters?
options: The cosine of two dense neural vectors
One point for every token in the document, including unmatched tokens
The sum of query count times matching document count for each query token
The reciprocal rank of the document
questions.explanation: The loop adds q_weight * d_sparse.get(tok, 0) for each token in the sparse query.

questions.question: What tuple shape does rrf_fuse return for each fused document?
options: (fused score, document index)
(query token, document length)
(rank, raw embedding vector)
(document index, fused score)
questions.explanation: The final sorted list comes from scores.items(), where each item is (idx, accumulated score).
